source_text: Hac atque huius modi facultate multa daemones futura praenuntiant, cum tamen ab eis longe sit altitudo illius prophetiae, quam deus per sanctos angelos et prophetas operatur. nam si quid de illa dei dispositione praenuntiant, audiunt. ut praenuntient; et cum ea praedicunt, quae inde audiunt, non fallunt neque falluntur; ueracissima enim sunt angelica et prophetica oracula. sic autem indignanter accipitur, quod aliqua etiam talia daemones audiant et praedicant, quasi aliquid indignum sit, ut quod ideo dicitur, ut hominibus innotescat, hoc non solum boni, uerum etiam mali non taceant. cum in ipsis hominibus etiam uitae bonae praecepta uideamus pariter a iustis peruersisque cantari, non obesse aliquid, immo etiam prodesse ad maiorem notitiam famamque ueritatis, cum de illa etiam hi quidquid nouerunt dicunt, qui ei peruersis moribus contradicunt. in ceteris autem suis praedicationibus daemones plerumque falluntur et fallunt. falluntur quidem, quia, cum suas dispositiones praenuntiant, ex inprouiso de- . super aliquid iubetur, quod eorum consilia cuncta perturbet. uelut si aliquid disponant quilibet homines quibusque potestatibus subditi, quod non prohibituros suos praepositos arbitrentur idque facturos se esse promittant, at illi, penes quos maior potestas est, ex alio superiore consilio hoc totum dispositum atque praeparatum repente prohibeant. falluntur etiam in causis naturalibus — sicut medici et nautae et agricolae, sed longe acutius longeque praestantius pro aerii corporis sensu sollertiore et exercitatiore praenoscunt — quia et haec ab angelis deo summo pie seruientibus ex alia dispositione ignota daemonibus ex inprouiso ac repente mutantur. tamquam si aliquid aegro extrinsecus accidat, quo moriatur, quem medicus ueris salutis praecedentibus signis uicturum esse promiserat; aut si aeris qualitate praeuisa diu flaturum illum uentum nautarum aliqui praedixissent, cui dominus Christus cum discipulis nauigans, ut quiesceret, imperauit, et facta est tranquillitas magna; uel si agricola illo anno fructificaturam uitem aliquam polliceatur, naturam utique terrae et numerum seminum callens, quo tamen anno eam uel inprouisa caeli intemperies arefaciat uel aliqua iussio potentioris eradicet: ita multa etiam ad praescientiam praedictionemque daemonum pertinentia, quae minoribus et usitatioribus causis futura praeuidentur, eadem maioribus et occultioribus causis inpedita mutantur. fallunt autem etiam studio fallendi et inuida uoluntate, qua hominum errore laetantur. sed ne apud cultores suos pondus auctoritatis amittant, id agunt, ut interpretibus suis signorumque suorum coniectoribus culpa tribuatur, quando uel decepti fuerint uel mentiti.
thought_title: Demons' predictions are limited and often false
orientation: Augustine is contrasting the limited, often mistaken predictions of demons with the true prophecy that God works through angels and prophets.
pass_a_gloss: By this and by a faculty of this kind demons announce many future things, although the height of that prophecy is far from them, which God works through holy angels and prophets. For if they announce anything from that disposition of God, they hear it so that they may announce it; and when they predict those things which they hear from there, they do not deceive and are not deceived; for angelic and prophetic oracles are most true. But it is received indignantly that demons also hear and predict some such things, as if it were something unworthy that what is said for this purpose, so that it may become known to human beings, this not only good men but also evil men should not keep silent. Since in human beings themselves we see the precepts of a good life sung equally by the righteous and the perverse, that it does not harm anything, indeed even benefits for the greater knowledge and fame of the truth, when even those say whatever they know about it who contradict it by perverse morals. But in their other predictions demons are for the most part deceived and deceive. They are deceived indeed because, when they announce their own dispositions, something is suddenly commanded from above, which disturbs all their plans. As if any human beings subject to any powers should arrange something, which they think their superiors will not prohibit, and should promise that they will do it, but those, in whose hands there is greater power, from another higher counsel should suddenly prohibit this whole thing arranged and prepared. They are also deceived in natural causes—just as physicians and sailors and farmers, but far more keenly and far more excellently they know beforehand according to the more skilled and more practiced sense of an airy body—because these things also are suddenly and unexpectedly changed by angels piously serving the most high God from another disposition unknown to demons. As if something should happen to a sick man from outside, by which he dies, whom the physician had promised would live on the basis of true preceding signs of health; or if, having foreseen the quality of the air, some sailors had predicted that that wind would blow for a long time, which the Lord Christ, sailing with his disciples, commanded to be still, and a great calm was made; or if a farmer should promise that some vine would bear fruit in that year, knowing indeed the nature of the soil and the number of seeds, but in that year either an unexpected harshness of the sky should dry it up or some command of a more powerful person should uproot it: so many things also pertaining to the foreknowledge and prediction of demons, which are foreseen as future from lesser and more ordinary causes, are hindered by greater and more hidden causes and are changed. But they also deceive by zeal for deceiving and by an envious will, by which they rejoice in human error. But lest they lose the weight of authority among their worshippers, they act so that the blame is attributed to their interpreters and to the conjecturers of their signs, when they have either been deceived or have lied.

choices.why: Keeps the spatial metaphor of 'altitudo' as height, which Augustine uses to mark the distance between demonic prediction and true prophecy.

choices.english: they hear it so that they may announce it
choices.why: Preserves the purpose clause force of 'ut' and the distinction between hearing (receiving) and announcing (delivering).
rejected: they listen in order to predict

choices.english: they do not deceive and are not deceived
choices.why: Keeps the active/passive contrast of 'fallunt' and 'falluntur' explicit, which is central to Augustine's point about true prophecy.
rejected: they neither deceive nor are deceived
they are not false nor mistaken

choices.term: aerii corporis sensu sollertiore et exercitatiore
choices.english: according to the more skilled and more practiced sense of an airy body
choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'airy body' and keeps the comparative force of both adjectives, showing demons' natural advantage.
rejected: by the keener and more trained sense of their aerial body
through the more acute and exercised sense of an airy body

choices.english: by zeal for deceiving and by an envious will
choices.why: Renders 'studio' as 'zeal' to capture the deliberate eagerness, and keeps 'inuida uoluntate' as a separate motive.
rejected: by eagerness to deceive and by envious will
by the desire of deceiving and by jealous will

choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of 'pondus' (weight) which conveys the seriousness and influence demons fear losing.

pass_b_english: By this and similar abilities demons announce many future things beforehand, yet the height of that prophecy which God works through his holy angels and prophets remains far beyond them. For if they announce anything from God's own disposition, they hear it so that they may announce it; and when they proclaim what they hear from there, they do not deceive and are not deceived, for the oracles of angels and prophets are utterly true. But some people take it indignantly that demons also hear and proclaim certain things of this kind, as if it were somehow unworthy that what is spoken precisely so that it may become known to human beings should not be kept silent by the wicked as well as the good. After all, even among human beings we see the precepts of a good life sung equally by the righteous and the perverse, and this does no harm; in fact it even helps the truth become better known and more widely famed when those who contradict it by their perverse conduct still say whatever they know about it. In their other predictions, however, demons are for the most part deceived and deceive. They are deceived because, when they announce their own dispositions, something is suddenly commanded from above that throws all their plans into confusion. It is as if certain people subject to various authorities were to arrange something they thought their superiors would not forbid, and promise they would carry it out—and then those who hold greater power, acting on some higher counsel, suddenly forbid the whole thing that had been arranged and prepared. They are also deceived in natural causes—just as physicians, sailors, and farmers are, though the demons foresee far more keenly and far more excellently according to the more skilled and more practiced sense of an airy body—because these things too are suddenly and unexpectedly changed by angels who serve the supreme God in piety, acting from another disposition unknown to demons. It is as if something should happen to a sick man from outside that kills him, after a physician had promised on the basis of true preceding signs of health that he would live; or as if some sailors had predicted from the observed quality of the air that a certain wind would blow for a long time, and then the Lord Christ, sailing with his disciples, commanded it to be still, and a great calm came about (Matthew 8:26); or as if a farmer, skilled in the nature of the soil and the number of seeds, should promise that a certain vine would bear fruit that year, and then either an unexpected harshness of the sky should dry it up or some command of a higher power should uproot it. In the same way, many things that pertain to the foreknowledge and prediction of demons—things foreseen as future from lesser and more ordinary causes—are impeded and changed by greater and more hidden causes. They also deceive by zeal for deceiving and by an envious will, through which they rejoice in human error. But so that they do not lose the weight of authority among their worshipers, they make sure that the blame is assigned to their interpreters and the conjecturers of their signs whenever they have been deceived or have lied.

last_rejected.why: 'salutis' means 'of health/saving' but context is signs of recovery, not 'of health' as a genitive modifier of 'signs'
last_rejected.ruling: 'salutis' = 'of health/saving'; 'signis...salutis' = 'signs of health/recovery'. 'True preceding signs of health' captures this accurately.
